descriptionChirho: To wash one's entire body in water, especially for ritual purification in Levitical law or for personal hygiene (Qal intransitive/reflexive).
To wash an object, body part, or another person with water, such as washing hands, feet, entrails, or garments (Qal transitive).
To be washed by another, expressing the passive reception of washing or cleansing (Pual passive stem).
To wash oneself as a deliberate reflexive act, emphasizing the subject's initiative in cleansing (Hitpael reflexive stem).
